title: Equirectangular Still Sidecar Schema
description: Metadata generated alongside each 360° equirectangular still capture in raw_data/equirect_stills/still_XXXX.json

sequence.description: 1-based sequence index of the still in the capture session.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch time (UTC) when the still was triggered.

still_source.description: Camera model or capture source identifier (e.g., RICOH THETA X).

width.description: Pixel width of the equirectangular JPEG image.

height.description: Pixel height of the equirectangular JPEG image.

phone_transform.description: 4x4 column-major phone-to-world transform at the moment of capture.

cam_transform.description: 4x4 column-major 360° camera-to-world transform, composed from phone pose + baked rig profile at capture time.

camera_file_url.description: Source URI or path on the external camera device.

trigger_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds to trigger the shutter.

transfer_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds to download the image from the camera.

bytes.description: File size of the captured JPEG image in bytes.

camera_clock_offset_ms.description: Camera clock minus phone clock at scan start, milliseconds (+ = camera ahead), measured by catching a second tick of the camera's dateTimeZone. Add to a phone timestamp to compare against the camera's EXIF DateTimeOriginal (1 s resolution): shutter latency = EXIF_second(+offset window) - trigger tap. The camera drifts 1-7 s/day, so the offset is per scan, never reusable.

camera_clock_offset_unc_ms.description: Half-window uncertainty of camera_clock_offset_ms, milliseconds (poll gap at the tick plus half the HTTP round trip).

rig_calibration_source.description: Source of the rig calibration used for cam_transform. Consumers should test for the 'solved' PREFIX rather than an exact match: anything starting with 'solved' carries a fitted rig extrinsic, anything else is the mechanical prior.

rig_calibration_residual_px_rms.description: RMS reprojection error of the edge-cost calibration fit (solver <= 14 only), in pixels of the 512-wide working equirect. NOT comparable across scans with different still counts. Solver >= 15 (photometric) does not write this — see rig_calibration_zncc and rig_calibration_yaw_spread_deg.

rig_calibration_zncc.description: Trimmed-mean zero-normalized cross-correlation between keyframe-unprojected points and the still at the solved pose (solver >= 15). Higher is better; field range ~0.5-0.8. The photometric replacement for residual_px_rms.

rig_calibration_yaw_spread_deg.description: Max-minus-min of per-still yaw re-solves at the solved offset (solver >= 15) — the solve's honest confidence number, immune to being flattered by fewer inputs. Field range 1-4.5 deg healthy; solves past 15 deg are rejected and the prior ships instead.

rig_calibration_solver_version.description: Version of the rig solver that produced cam_transform. A bump forces a re-solve on the scan's next Process, which is how superseded calibrations self-heal.

rig_calibration_railed.description: Solved parameters that came back sitting on a bound of their search box, one human-readable phrase each. NON-EMPTY MEANS THE POSE IS APPROXIMATE: the optimizer ran out of model rather than converging on the data, and the residual is a boundary value, not a fit. Empty array is the healthy case; the key is written on every bake, so its ABSENCE means the producing build predates this field, not that nothing was railed.

rig_offset_phone_m.description: Rig offset from the phone camera to the 360 lens, in the PHONE's own frame (ARKit camera axes: +x right, +y up, -z view direction), metres. The rod runs along -x, so a 0.72 m rig is about [-0.72, 0, 0]. This is the geometry cam_transform was composed from: cam_position = phone_position + phone_rotation * rig_offset_phone_m.

rig_rod_length_m.description: Magnitude of rig_offset_phone_m — the phone-camera-to-lens distance along the rod, i.e. the quantity the operator measures with a tape.

rig_yaw_deg.description: Solved yaw of the 360 camera relative to the phone's horizontal forward, degrees. Note heading = -yaw.

rig_rod_anchor_m.description: Rod length (m) the calibration solve was ANCHORED on — the operator's tape entry at solve time, or the mechanical default. Compare with rig_rod_length_m (the solved value): a solve pinned against this anchor's bound means the tape and the data disagree, i.e. re-measure the rod.

rig_rod_anchor_source.description: Whether rig_rod_anchor_m came from the operator's measurement or the built-in default.

elevation_offset_deg.description: Uniform vertical registration offset between the equirect's rows and the latitude mapping, solved per scan (+ = image content sits lower than geometry predicts). Consumers sampling the equirect with the standard mapping should compensate by this much. This is a fitted nuisance parameter absorbing model error, not a measured camera property, and is expected to be retired.
